atoms.text: This is Sally the Seagull. Sally wants to teach you about physical geography by showing you around some coastlines.

instruction.text: Answer Sally’s question by listening to the options and selecting the correct answer.

atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>What is physical geography?</voice>

b.sound: Physical geography is the geography of anything natural, such as a beach or a lake!
Physical geography is the geography of human things, such as tall buildings.

instruction.text: This is Sanna Beach in Scotland. Select the sand to learn more.

feedback.end: Great work! Sanna Beach is a sandy beach. Behind the beach, we can see sand dunes, which are a natural defence against storms.

instruction.text: This is Hurst Spit in Hampshire. Select the lighthouse to learn more.

feedback.end: A spit is a narrow bit of land that sticks out into the sea. Let’s take a look at the beach!

instruction.text: This is the beach on Hurst Spit. Select the pebbles to learn more.

feedback.end: The beach at Hurst spit is a shingle or pebble beach. Shingle beaches are created by the sea washing pebbles onto the shore.

instruction.text: Let’s do some fieldwork! You and Sally are going to the beach using a phone map for directions. Answer Sally’s questions.

atoms.a: “Which direction is the beach from our location?”
atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>Which direction is the beach from our location?</voice>
ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>Which way will we have to turn?</voice>

feedback.end: Great! Fieldwork is what we do in geography to find things out. It can be using a map to get somewhere or measuring things like rainfall!

instruction.text: This is Ha Long Bay in Vietnam. Select the biggest island to learn more.

feedback.end: Good Spot! Ha Long Bay has lots of islands. The islands block all the waves from the open ocean, so the sea is much calmer here.
